title: Alternative Name
paragraphs: “I… I see.”
Father nodded, looking pained, in response to the man’s forceful assertion.
“I’ve verified this thoroughly, so it’s a fact. As expected, Takt has made enemies all over the place—he’s been using his power and influence to crush people, so he has a lot of enemies.”
Rivals are backing him up. It’s true that Takt’s reputation is nothing but a paper tiger—all surface and no substance.

While he did invent things and spread new products across the world, he didn’t give the slightest thought to merchants struggling because their existing products weren’t selling, so the merchants’ guild apparently viewed him as a threat. Of course, if anyone tried to sabotage him, he’d crush them completely, make a spectacle of them, and then confiscate their assets. He does grant some benefits to workers, but he forces them into backbreaking labor while creating the illusion that their lives have improved. And then there’s the “corporate slave” drink.

This mindset is the exact opposite of Father’s approach to business and governance. After all, Father’s approach was to make a profit without burdening existing resources. He adjusted his profit margins to prevent prices from falling too low, making it difficult to create enemies. As for the bio-plants, I’ve heard he provided them to farmers free of charge, but designed them to wither if they weren’t properly cared for and the soil wasn’t managed correctly.

In Takt’s case, the theory seemed to be to use his inventions to devour existing resources so thoroughly that not a single blade of grass or tree could grow. However, there was no follow-up support for the barren land left behind. It’s no wonder he has so many enemies.

It seems this man was also a hindrance to Takt in that line of business, and Takt found a pretext to pick a fight with him. Since the nuisance was conveniently in a bind, Takt probably took the opportunity to provoke him. According to the man, while he was struggling to find a cure for his wife’s illness, his daughter from his previous marriage was apparently won over. Since she’s his ex-wife’s daughter, she was a pretty little piglet—apparently right up Takt’s alley—so it seems both mother and daughter ended up joining Takt’s harem.
What an outrageous story about pigs.

I wonder if Takt possesses some kind of pheromone that attracts pigs like this? ……Come to think of it, maybe I had pheromones like that too, before I awakened to true love. Otherwise, there’s no way so many pigs would have swarmed around me like that.
“I’m lucky just to be alive. Many of those who might have become my comrades were killed by Takt and the traitors.”
I suppose so. In the previous loop, a merchant from Zeltoble was assassinated. That’s the kind of mischief Takt and his pig-like lot are causing all over the world.
“That’s a terrible story. What a bunch of despicable pigs.”

It’s standard practice for pigs to switch partners the moment a more convenient man comes along. Pigs are extremely skilled at camouflage, so the men aren’t at fault. That’s just the nature of pigs. Proof of this is that whenever something doesn’t go their way, they immediately get sulky and grumble “oink oink,” yet they have absolutely no intention of actually doing anything about it.
To top it off, they scheme to manipulate men. If there’s something you want them to do, just say it clearly!
Honesty is a virtue! That’s why I’m honest! Father is honest, too!
Oh? It feels like Father from the first world is taking a step back, as if to say, “No… that’s just you,” but… he really is humble, isn’t he! See what I mean?
“Ah… well, how should I put it? It’s a pretty awful story, isn’t it…”
“Mm-hmm. It might sound strange coming from me, a woman, but I agree—it is an awful story.”
“What about the possibility of brainwashing by the Takt faction? I heard they were doing that sort of thing, too?”
Zou asks.

“Of course, Gaelion also noted that it’s a possibility, but if the fox from the Takt faction has been taken out, I think it’s unlikely. That creature is a monster that induces hallucinations, but even without it, they’re still mingling with the ones lying low, so I think those are their true feelings.”
“It’s hopeless, isn’t it…”
“I’d like to think the problem lay with that mother’s upbringing.”
Éclair says this while resting her hand on her head. That’s too naive. A pig is born a pig, you know.
“They’re just pigs, after all.”
“Yes, just as the Spear Hero says, let’s make those pigs pay. The means don’t matter. That is the greatest joy for me… no, for us.”
“Ugh… her eyes are dead… I understand her feelings all too well, but… women are scary… to be able to switch partners so easily…”
“That’s right. Pigs are ugly.”
I’ll need Father to deeply understand this point. Just as I was thinking that, Éclair said to Father:
“Mr. Iwatani, please understand that not all women in the world are like that…”

“I bet it was more like, ‘Rather than supporting my boring criminal husband, maybe I should switch to that exciting, rich, whip-wielding hero who pays attention to me!’ Doesn’t that sound like a good deal?”

Panda is reading the pig’s mind. I’m sure he’s spot on. The fact that he calls steady, reliable people “boring” and describes selfish jerks as “exciting” is proof that he truly understands the Pig. As expected of a mercenary—he’s got quite the analytical skills.
“Rasa…”
“I’ll pass on that, though. I don’t like that sort of thing. Money’s only worth anything if you earn it yourself. Elmelo, you feel the same way, don’t you?”

While the panda is chatting with the elephant like this, Father looks troubled. Well, there was a similar flashy mammoth at the elephant’s old family home, after all. The elephant should understand perfectly well.
“It’s okay!”
“Gaelion-chan?”
“Gaelion has sworn to love Naofumi even after the world ends. Dragons are persistent, so he won’t be switching partners. And those who love Naofumi won’t change either.”
“Ah… yeah. Thanks.”
A Rival is trying to score points here, so I’ll cut them off.
“The Takt remnants have no right to live anyway. If we can find them, we’ll grant that wish.”
After all, it’s a foregone conclusion that the Takt remnants are headed straight to the Pig King of Faubrey. We need to send them to the meat processing plant as soon as possible.
“Yes! Please take care of it!”
And so, we ended up heading out to wipe out the Takt remnants.
“That’s right! The island’s likely to become a battlefield, so you’d better not come. But I’ll make sure Gaelion’s satisfied, so just wait and see.”
As he said that, Rival flashed the video crystal at the man. As if he’d understood, the man bowed his head and stepped back.
“I’ll leave it to you.”
And so, we set out for our destination, leading our team with us.
“How should I put it… you can see the building even from a distance. There seem to be spots with strong currents along the way here, but I’m surprised we didn’t miss it.”
We turned our gaze from the ship toward the island. There appeared to be a spot that looked like a harbor where we could dock, and beyond it stood what looked like a mansion.
“It seems to be a place that Takt secretly built and turned into a resort, hiding it from all relevant parties.”
“Huh… I wonder why he kept it a secret?”
“Well, it’s Takt, after all.”
Maybe he was thinking in some strange way we just couldn’t understand. After all, Takt is a reincarnated being. Their goal is to corrupt and bring this world to ruin.

“I get the feeling that doesn’t really answer the question… but well, on the surface, he was billed as a genius the world takes pride in, so maybe he just wanted to spread his wings without worrying about what others thought.”
“It seems he liked to keep all sorts of things under wraps.”
So Takt is that fake genius with a shiny veneer. But no matter how dazzling that veneer may be, it’s already starting to peel away in tatters.
“By the way, there’s a rumor that besides that conspicuous mansion, there’s another one hidden deep within the island.”

“Really? It kind of feels like… the sort of place where a ‘closed circle’ mystery might unfold. Especially since it’s an island with some ominous legends attached to it. What do you call it? It’d make a great movie title—something like *The Seven-Split Island Murder Case*.”
“Is that so?”
“It’s the kind of plot twist you’d expect on an island owned by the wealthy.”
“Motoyasu-kun, you seem like the type who’d run into something like that, don’t you?”
Father asks, sounding a bit amused.
“I have, in fact, found myself caught up in the turmoil of a wealthy family’s troublesome power struggle.”

During what was supposed to be a relaxing summer vacation, I got dragged into a messy family feud involving the Pig family. Looking back now, that was a real hassle. And when it all came down to it, it turned out to be a bit of a letdown—the “Pig” family members actually cared about each other but just weren’t on the same page. In the end, we all laughed it off.
“Still, it was only on the level of the commotion when I transferred to a rural school, so it didn’t leave much of an impression.”
Back then, I thought I was starting fresh, so I made a big fuss and threw myself into solving the case with those pigs, but I feel like I ended up acting in a rather casual, matter-of-fact way.
“Speaking of islands, I once went to a large island that felt more like a resort town.”

Although it was a distance from the main island of Japan, I did transfer to a place that was sort of like a city. It was advertised as a place where you could have mysterious experiences thanks to the island’s unique science and technology.

“It wasn’t quite on Ren’s level, but their own cutting-edge technology was the main attraction. I’m not an expert, so I didn’t understand a thing—it was just a tourist spot, after all. Besides, I wasn’t enrolled there for very long.”
Honestly, looking back, my student life involved moving around way too much. It’s a wonder my grades didn’t drop with all that.
“Hmm… Maybe Motoyasu-kun’s world was actually pretty sci-fi too. They probably just call superpowers and Magic by different names.”
“Was there something like that? Though, I do picture that pig—I just can’t remember where I met him. What kind of guy was he again? I can’t remember him just by his face.”
No matter how hard I try, I just can’t remember. Well, it’s probably no big deal. It’s just that pig, after all. He’s not worth remembering.
“Secretly existing supernatural abilities or Magic—maybe their memories were erased when they left that place… The scary thing about Motoyasu-kun is that you can’t rule it out.”
“HAHAHA! My world isn’t the world of Itsuki, you know? That’s not the case at all.”
“Well, the plot where supernatural abilities and Magic exist in a hidden world is a classic trope in subculture. Since there’s no way to prove it, worrying about it is a losing battle.”
I feel like Fathers—who couldn’t protect me from a false accusation—would point out that I should care at least a little, but I should look ahead rather than dwell on that!
“It’s a little frustrating that I can’t understand what Naofumi and the others are saying. I want to do my best so I can understand Gaelion’s stories too.”
“Boo.”
By the way, Sakura-chan is, of course, right here with us, keeping an eye out to make sure our Rival doesn’t pull any stunts, so she’s protesting. Keep it up, Sakura-chan.
“From what I’ve picked up here and there, are they covering up a murder? Isn’t that something Takt used to do all the time?”
“Well, it’s similar in a way, but I guess it’s different. Anyway, I think this is going to be the decisive battle against Takt’s remnants, so everyone, let’s stay on our toes!”
“Right!”
“Of course!”
At Father’s words, everyone on board—including me, Sakura-chan, the Éclairs, and the rest—nods in agreement.
“I’m itching to get into action… I was getting sick and tired of constantly being on guard, wondering when they’d show up. I’d like to put an end to this right here.”

“It’s only natural to make those who killed the Hero, covered it up, and even started a war for their own selfish revenge pay the price. I’ll pay the price for Melromarc’s involvement on the Queen’s behalf!”
“I really want to bring peace to the world as soon as possible.”
Panda, Éclair, and Zou are showing their determination, too.
“We’ll be the ones to slaughter those evil ones who treat the world like a toy!”
Led by Yuki-chan’s voice, the Filolial-sama I brought along are joining in too. We’re already fully prepared. We’re about to go on a pig hunt for the remnants of Takt!

“Father, as a preemptive strike, should I launch an attack—like a ‘Liberation Firestorm’—that’ll completely reshape the island?　Or maybe the Liberation Meltblast, which is still in development? Hell, even blowing the island to smithereens would be fine.”
“Spear Hero, in your own words, that’s a no-go because you can’t capture the pigs.”
“I didn’t ask for your opinion!”

“Um, Motoyasu-kun, as Gaelion-chan said, one of our goals is to capture the remaining Takt members, so please don’t blow the island to smithereens. You know… we’ll need to make them spill the beans on where they’re hiding the money they stole.”
“Got it. So we’ll capture them alive, one by one, and deal with them.”
“U-uh, yeah…”

And so, we landed on our target island—Seven Island, as Takt had renamed it—and charged toward the mansion. We’re cutting through the lavish garden. There’s some kind of monument carved from stone that looks like a memorial. I thought it might be something like what was on Cal Mira Island, but it seems different.
“What is this?”
“Looks like it’s written with the island’s fairy tale.”
“Oh, the one about splitting the Demon King into seven pieces and burying them?”
“That’s right. It looks like they’ve recorded each one in great detail. It even has some gruesome details written there, like ‘Tear off his right hand,’ and such.”
It says the Demon King first demanded a human sacrifice. And it seems the first hero pierced the Demon King’s belly.
“Is this just Takt’s sense of humor or something? Or was it here all along?”
“I don’t think we need to worry about it.”
“You’re right. Let’s hurry on.”
So, we pressed on, but there wasn’t a trace of those pigs. I don’t know if they’re lurking in the mansion or hiding somewhere on the island, but it’s time to storm in!
“Here we go!”
The Filolial-sama followed right behind me, and we’ve successfully taken over the harbor and the area around the gardens!
“It’s impressive to see so many of us here, but…”
“Security isn’t just thin—it’s practically nonexistent… I’ve got a bad feeling about this.”
Fathers said this with a hint of caution.
“No matter what happens, I’ll show you I can handle it!”
And with that, we arrived at the mansion’s front entrance with plenty of time to spare.
“Now, let’s smash our way in and make a grand entrance!”
“Hold on a sec. Spear Hero.”
That’s when Panda stops me right in front of the entrance.
